scope: sampled-only: actual visual inspection of nine saved final-frame PNGs from three moving test sequences; not a video or every-frame visual review

findings: Reconstruction visibly reduces the dense speckling on timber arches, paving and planted surroundings.
The open pavilion axis, crossed arch layers, pale caps and skyline framing remain readable in all three images.

The reconstructed deck shadows and small timber surface detail are softer than the independent 128-SPP reference. The reference remains sharper; this is a quality limitation rather than evidence of exact detail recovery.
remainingLimits: Segmented arch geometry and simplified foliage are shared scene-model features, not denoiser defects.
Some distant facade noise remains in the reconstructed sample.

findings: The same white/warm windows and yellow, blue, purple and magenta seasonal lamps remain visible in raw, reconstructed and reference images.
Reconstruction reduces grain on the building, bench, ground and lit tree canopy while retaining the arrangement of individual string lights and arches.
Small bright samples remain on the lawn/path and in the independent reference. This saved frame does not establish that moving night illumination is free of flicker.
remainingLimits: Roof/brick/ground detail is smoother in reconstructed output than in the reference.
Most unlit foliage remains dark as part of the authored selective night lighting.

findings: The curved roof framing, transparent glass, visible palms and corner masonry remain aligned and recognizable across all three images.
Reconstruction reduces lawn and stone-base noise; the fine glasshouse framing remains present.
The reconstructed pale-stone joints, brick cap and shadow boundary are noticeably softer than in the 128-SPP reference. Fine stochastic noise remains within portions of the glazing.
remainingLimits: This is an exterior glazing sample with visible planting; it does not certify a navigable surveyed Conservatory interior.
Reflection/transmission clarity is assessed only at this saved camera pose.

measuredEvidence.measurement: Display-space RGB RMSE against independent high-sample references; second half of each moving sequence. Temporal residual is consecutive error difference, with reference motion subtracted, not raw image difference.
measuredEvidence.pairing: Raw and reconstructed presentations share one trace accumulation, acceleration structure and scene-time update; the high-SPP reference remains independent.

limits: Only frame index 31 of each 32-frame sequence is visually inspected here. The temporal-reduction numbers come from the separate numerical sequence test, not from watching these stills.
Test images are 640x400 at 8 current samples per frame; the independent reference uses 128 samples and still has finite sampling error. They are not final exported movie frames.
Visible smoothing of narrow shadow/stone/timber detail remains. Passing numerical error thresholds does not imply all fine detail is identical to the reference.
No FPS claim, complete-route review, temporal ghosting guarantee or current real-world seasonal-display claim is made.
